title: What's Really Clogging Your Kitchen Sink Drain?
description: Slow-draining kitchen sinks are most frequently caused by a buildup of cooking fats, oils, and grease inside the P-trap. When poured warm down the drain, liquid fats quickly cool and coat the interior pipe walls, catching food scraps and coffee grounds over time until water flow stops completely. In bathroom sinks, hair and soap scum form a similar fibrous obstruction. Prevent blockages by scraping grease into food waste containers instead of washing it down the sink. If water begins backing up, manually removing and clearing the P-trap is far safer for your plumbing system than relying on caustic chemical drain cleaners.
image_prompt: A crisp, eye-level vertical 9:16 photograph inside a modern residential kitchen cabinet beneath a sink. A plumber wearing blue nitrile gloves holds the lower curve of a disassembled white PVC tubular P-trap. Inside the opened P-trap weir, a realistic buildup of solidified grease and soft organic food debris is visible, clearly showing the source of a drainage blockage. The waste tailpiece extends correctly down from a stainless steel sink strainer, and the trap arm aligns horizontally toward the waste pipe in the back wall. A small plastic bucket sits below the open joint to catch residual water. Bright interior cabinet lighting, sharp focus on the clogged pipe interior, wet textures, realistic PVC fittings, slip nuts, and rubber washers. Professional commercial photography, vertical framing, strictly realistic plumbing layout.
